job.title: Care Coordinator- Aged Care
job.description:
Pathway Talent is partnering with an established and respected not-for-profit organisation to recruit an experienced Care Coordinator for its aged care team.

About the Organisation
Our client delivers person-centred support across aged care, disability, mental health and community services. Its aged care team works with older people, their families and carers to help customers live independently at home and stay connected to their communities.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Service Delivery Manager, you’ll coordinate services under the Support at Home program. You’ll visit customers at home, develop care plans with them and work with families, carers and clinicians as their needs change. You’ll also supervise frontline staff across multiple locations and work with Rostering and Allocations to match the right staff to each customer’s needs.

What You’ll Do

Care Coordination and Team Support

  • Develop and review individualised care plans that reflect each participant’s goals, cultural needs, preferences and assessed supports.
  • Set and review quarterly budgets and help participants understand which services they can access and what contributions they may need to make.
  • Supervise and mentor frontline staff, support new starters through induction and identify training needs.
  • Coordinate service bookings and work with Rostering and Allocations to manage absences, cancellations and short-notice changes.
  • Refer clinical concerns to qualified clinicians and make sure their recommendations are reflected in care plans and day-to-day supports.
  • Maintain accurate care records and contribute to incident reporting, quality reviews and service improvements.

Business Development and Referral Growth

  • Identify cross-referral opportunities from NDIS, mental health and community programs, and follow up with Commonwealth Home Support Programme (CHSP) clients who have been reassessed for Support at Home.
  • Build referral relationships with GPs, pharmacies, hospital discharge planners, care finders, assessment organisations, retirement villages, seniors groups, and Aboriginal and culturally diverse community organisations.
  • Engage people who have been assigned Support at Home funding and are choosing a provider, as well as former Home Care Package recipients who have transitioned to Support at Home and want to change providers.
  • Represent the organisation at expos, community events and information sessions. Explain how Support at Home works, what services cost and how to choose a provider.
  • Explain the organisation’s fee-for-service options to people who want to access services while waiting for an assessment or funding.

Referral, Intake and Onboarding

  • Accept and action referrals through the My Aged Care provider portal. Contact participants promptly to help them start services within the timeframe specified in their notice.
  • Review each participant’s Notice of Decision, classification level and support plan, including any approved Restorative Care or End-of-Life pathway or Assistive Technology and Home Modifications (AT-HM) supports.
  • Explain service prices, participant contributions, the care management deduction and monthly statements so participants can make informed decisions and give informed consent.
  • Onboard third-party providers, such as podiatrists, allied health practitioners, and home maintenance and gardening providers, using the organisation’s price list and approved purchase orders.

Key Performance Indicators

  • Referral growth and conversion from internal programs and external referral partners.
  • Timely contact with referred participants and service commencement within the timeframe specified in their notice.
  • Timely completion of service agreements, initial care plans and quarterly budgets, with accurate records in Lumary.
  • Timely clinical referrals and follow-through on recommendations


What You’ll Bring

  • Preffered Qualification : Diploma in Community Services, or Enrolled Nurse, or equivalent experience in aged care.
  • Essential: Minimum experience of 3 years as aged care coordinator or care partner
  • A strong understanding of the Support at Home program
  • Experience coordinating person-centred services and supervising or mentoring frontline teams.
  • An understanding of aged care quality standards and experience working with clinical, rostering and operational teams.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and exercise sound judgement.
  • A current NSW driver licence
  • NDISWSC
  • WWCC
  • Police Check (Issued within 3 months)

Why Consider This Opportunity?

  • Competitive salary and autonomy in your day-to-day work, with the opportunity to shape how aged care services are delivered.
  • Generous salary packaging through not-for-profit benefits that may increase your take-home pay.
  • Fitness Passport with discounted access to participating gyms, fitness centres and swimming pools.
  • Flexible working arrangements subject to operational requirements.
  • Additional leave options through purchased annual leave arrangements.
  • Employee Assistance Program with confidential counselling and wellbeing support.
  • Professional development opportunities to expand your skills and grow your career.
  • Purpose-driven work that helps older people maintain their independence and stay connected to their communities.
  • Collaborative environment where you’ll work alongside supportive teams committed to delivering quality services.

Apply Now
